Definition: a vacuity, i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin
BiblicalUsage: Without form is the word for emptiness, a void, a waste — and it appears three times, in the beginning and in two judgments. In Genesis 1:2 the earth was without form, and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep. In Isaiah 34:11 God stretches out upon Edom the line of confusion and the stones of emptiness. And in Jeremiah 4:23 the prophet says, I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void, and the heavens, and they had no light.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the void in Genesis is the promise inside the judgment: the earth was without form, and then God spoke, and form came. What is empty in his hands does not stay empty.
